title: RF-DETR vs YOLOv9: where the frontier crosses
dek: The frontier crosses: YOLOv9 wins the small end and runs 22.8% faster, while RF-DETR tops out at 58.6 mAP on an RTX 5070 Ti.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: At matched compute on an RTX 5070 Ti, neither family wins outright. YOLOv9 is more accurate per parameter at the small end and 22.8% faster on average in PyTorch; RF-DETR pulls ahead on accuracy at the large end, topping out at 58.6 mAP against YOLOv9's 57.1. Across 4 nearest-parameter pairs the accuracy split is even, 2 to 2, with YOLOv9 averaging 1.5 mAP points higher overall.
RF-DETR fields 4 measured variants; YOLOv9 fields 4. Both run the same COCO val2017 protocol at 640 px on an RTX 5070 Ti, so the two ladders align by parameter count.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. Every RF-DETR and YOLOv9 variant highlighted against the full set.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent. Pairing by nearest parameter count, the two families split the 4 pairs 2 and 2, and YOLOv9 averages 1.5 mAP points higher overall. The result depends on size class: YOLOv9-C leads the lower pairs, while RF-DETR-L reaches 58.6 mAP at the top, above YOLOv9-C's 57.1.
YOLOv9 is faster at matched compute: 22.8% faster on average in PyTorch FP32. RF-DETR's most accurate variant, RF-DETR-L, runs 25.1 FPS against YOLOv9-C at 42.3.

The accuracy lead changes hands with model size. At the small end YOLOv9 leads: its parameter-efficient variants sit above RF-DETR's smallest, RF-DETR-N, which needs 30.47M parameters to reach 51.4 mAP. At the large end RF-DETR leads, with RF-DETR-L at 58.6 mAP. There is no single winner; the choice follows your size class.

items.v: Both families ship under permissive licenses

blocks.text: Pick YOLOv9 for small and mid-size deployments and for raw throughput: it is faster on average and more parameter-efficient at the small end. Pick RF-DETR when peak accuracy matters and you can run a larger model, since it reaches 58.6 mAP at the top of the measured range. Both ship under permissive licenses. See the per-variant specs on the RF-DETR and YOLOv9 model pages.
